content.value_statement: Teams can introduce conflicting frameworks, services, or build tools when stack decisions are scattered. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to follow documented technology standards.
actual_capabilities: Guides technology choices against the project's documented stack standards.
Helps evaluate new libraries, frameworks, and dependencies for consistency.
Supports framework-specific implementation decisions for common web stacks.
Frames database, ORM, testing, build, and deployment choices.
Prompts consistent decisions for authentication and third-party service integrations.
limitations: The skill depends on a referenced tech stack file outside SKILL.md.
It does not install packages, run tests, or verify code by itself.
It does not replace security, license, or maintenance review for new dependencies.
It may be incomplete when the referenced standards file is unavailable.

use_cases.title: Review Dependency Choices
use_cases.description: Compare a proposed library with project standards before adding it to the application.

use_cases.title: Keep Architecture Consistent
use_cases.description: Check new service, database, and framework decisions against approved stack guidance.

use_cases.title: Support Stack Onboarding
use_cases.description: Help new contributors understand which tools and patterns the project expects.

prompt_templates.title: Check Stack Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-tech-stack to review whether [library] fits this project. Compare it with the current stack standards and list concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Implementation Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-tech-stack to choose tools for [feature]. Recommend options that match the existing frameworks, testing tools, and build process.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Service Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-tech-stack to plan an integration with [service]. Identify stack conventions, required configuration areas, and review risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Stack Change Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Use global-tech-stack to audit this stack change: [proposal]. Compare it with approved standards and recommend accept, revise, or reject.

output_examples.input: Can we add a new payment SDK for checkout?
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use the approved payment provider unless requirements demand another SDK. Risks include vendor overlap, duplicated webhooks, and compliance review.

output_examples.input: Which test framework should cover a new API route?
output_examples.output: Use the project's existing API test framework. Add integration coverage for route behavior and avoid introducing a second runner.

output_examples.input: Should this service use a new database?
output_examples.output: Start with the approved database unless scale, data shape, or compliance needs justify a change. Document tradeoffs before adoption.

best_practices: Check the referenced stack standards before adding a dependency.
Document why a new tool is necessary when the approved stack is insufficient.
Keep implementation choices aligned with existing framework and testing patterns.
anti_patterns: Introducing a second framework for a problem already solved by the stack.
Choosing a dependency before checking project standards and maintenance status.
Using the skill as approval for risky authentication or payment changes.

faq.question: Does this skill make technology decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant to compare options with documented stack standards.

faq.question: Can it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only; installation requires a separate user action.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information does it rely on?
faq.answer: It relies on SKILL.md and the referenced global tech stack standards.

faq.question: Can it evaluate security risk for new libraries?
faq.answer: It can raise consistency concerns, but it does not replace security review.

faq.question: What happens if the standards file is missing?
faq.answer: The assistant should ask for the missing stack standards or use available project context.
